purpose: TASK-G04 golden A/B + class-blind re-score: shipped single-question payload vs G02 atomic six-question payload, two interleaved passes per named Jev release. Evidence only; no production flip.
key_loading: The TypeSafe API key environment variable was read from the maintainer's main-checkout .env via python-dotenv dotenv_values and passed to the child process environment only. No credential value (or credential variable name) appears in any artifact, stdout, or log.

method.corpus: tests/eval/evalsets/blackwall_security.evalset.json (187, TASK-F09 balanced) + blackwall_evasion_proof.evalset.json (10) = 197 cases. These are the class-blind, label-free shared-template states pinned by tests/unit/test_class_blind_evalset.py, so this single run set is both the golden A/B and the class-blind re-score; the historical 157+10 runs in tests/eval/results/jev_runs* remain the baseline.
method.arms: legacy = shipped single is_threat noul over build_legacy_state (byte-identical to canonical scorer, asserted by the recomputation test); atomic = six G02 noul questions over the native-object build_state with the G03-refined unauthorized_access criterion; code combines with fail-closed max.
method.releases: Requested by name (jev-1.13.0, jev-1.14.0), never the moving alias; served_model recorded per row and checked to equal the request.
method.interleaving: pass 1/2 -> release 1.13/1.14 -> arm legacy/atomic (releases and arms interleaved within each pass)
method.metrics: Repo methodology (test_jev_class_blind_runs_data.py): clear_high => predicted malicious, clear_low => benign, in-band [0.08,0.40] => escalate (Tier-2 fire proxy); accuracy on decided cases, recall on malicious, AUROC pairwise, ECE 10-bin, FRR on benign. Disagreement-route Tier-2 (novelty >=0.4 with P<0.2) is not modeled by this Tier-1-only harness, so escalation is the in-band share only.
method.gates: F10 re-baselined on held-out: accuracy >=0.85, recall >=0.75, AUROC >=0.97, ECE <=0.27, in-band escalation <=20%, FRR <5%, evasion <10%. Every figure recomputed from per-case answers, never from stored scores/bands.
method.discarded_note: No run discarded: all 8x197 calls returned HTTP 200 with no fallback rows and served the requested release. No 429/529 was observed.

generated_at_provenance: artifact generated_at is a UTC ISO-8601 instant emitted by scripts/jev_g04_ab.py at export time.

held_out_misses.description: Held-out benign cases scored clear_high by the atomic arm in pass 1, with the single category that triggered the fail-closed max. These are the benign-side misses that feed TASK-F10/F02; no per-case patching was applied.

decision.rationale: NO-GO. On held-out cases the legacy arm passes all five re-baselined F10 gates (accuracy, recall, AUROC, ECE, in-band escalation) plus FRR, while the atomic arm additionally fails AUROC (~0.79-0.82 vs >=0.97), escalation (~41-46% vs <=20%), FRR (~90-100% vs <5%) and accuracy on 3 of 4 runs. The fail-closed max amplifies isolated benign category hits (benign auth/network calls score 0.94-0.96 on credential_theft), so Tier-1 clears almost no benign traffic; this is the benign-side cost ADR 0009 Open Item 3 predicted from F02. IMPORTANT: the retained evasion-rate gate (<10%) FAILS for BOTH arms (2 of 6 held-out evasion-proof cases per run, 33.3%, both plain C2 beacons with no attack text) — this is the known C2/IOC weakness ADR 0009 names, not an atomic-specific regression. Keep the legacy payload; record both the benign and evasion misses for F10/F02. No src/ or rulebook change ships with this task.

caveats: Tier-1 signals only, not full-firewall verdicts; Tier-2 fire rate is the in-band escalation share, not a measured Gemini call count.

The 101-case held-out split is deterministic and label-blind but exploratory: these cases were inspected during F10's band tuning (ADR 0009 OI4), so this is not independent confirmation. Both arms are scored on the identical split, so the A/B comparison itself is matched.
One day, two named releases, two passes each; atomic spread is larger than legacy (zone changes 6-7 vs 2-3) but the gate failures are far outside spread.
The G03-refined unauthorized_access criterion is included; the dominant atomic false-hold drivers are credential_theft / exfiltration / unauthorized_access on benign calls, not that one wording.
No band change was made. F10's interim 0.08/0.40 edges remain in force; if Track G ever lands, re-run scripts/jev_band_sweep.py on these runs before treating the edges as final.

The retained evasion gate fails for both arms on held-out (33.3%, 2/6 plain C2-beacon cases), so neither arm can be said to pass 'every gate'; only the five F10-rebaselined gates plus FRR pass on legacy.

question_definitions and per-row is_fallback were captured in the driver for future runs; on this artifact they were backfilled deterministically from the unchanged source constants and from the fact that all 1,576 calls succeeded (is_fallback=false on every row).
